races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Timurshah
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins in good-ground hurdles heading into this, latest over C&D conditions, with trainer Aidan Melia in decent 14-day form (1/3); hold-up style suits if pace is genuine and he returns quickly off just 6 days rest.

runners_data.name: My Trump Card
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old whose best form came on ground easier than good — sole good-ground run (1/14) produced no impact, and a 100-day absence for McConnell's string (0/27 T14) makes confidence hard to find.

runners_data.name: Tassarolo
runners_data.note: Hogan runner fitted with a tongue-strap who holds good-ground form (10/15 sim-going) but all five recent runs came at shorter trips; the step up to 2m½f is the key query and the hold-up style needs a genuine pace to exploit.

runners_data.name: Teed Up
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who wears a tongue-tie and carries a ⚠ fade flag — Mullins saddles a horse 2 days since last run, and the recent form string of 80000 is hard to upgrade; Galway's undulating finish will test the stamina reserves here.

runners_data.name: Playtime
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott five-year-old with a fine good-ground record (9/15, 1W4P) including a C&D runner-up and two further places at similar trips; hold-up style and the Elliott/Williamson combination give this genuine each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Barrys Spirit
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on good ground at OR 112 last season — true running style is a deep closer, but the race map has him in midfield given the volume of hold-up types; 246-day absence is the principal concern, and the style-fit discount (0.92) applies.

runners_data.name: Castleheath
runners_data.note: Raced to a win at 10f on good ground at OR 112 but all strong form came over much shorter; a 216-day layoff compounds the concern and though he is a genuine hold-up horse his chance here relies on conditions he has not recently met — mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear.

runners_data.name: Cloonainra
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner and the pivot around which the entire pace map revolves; OR 112 and placed twice from nine good-ground runs (2W4P), but placed well below his own best in six of his last seven — his value is tactical dominance, not class.

runners_data.name: Bannow Blaze
runners_data.note: A proper hold-up type who has won over 16f on good ground and finished second at higher OR, but falls in a race with multiple closers competing for the same ground; mapped to midfield by necessity, and a 55-day absence after an unseating and fall sequence (UF) adds risk.

runners_data.name: Wahraan
runners_data.note: Won over 18f good ground just four days ago — back extremely quickly for Bedi, who has no T14 form — and the tongue-tie combination with a proven staying profile on good ground makes this a live candidate if the quick turnaround is not a concern.

runners_data.name: Mo Ghille Mar
runners_data.note: John Joe Hanlon five-year-old who won over 17f good ground and has three wins and three places on similar conditions (11/15); fitted with a hood, and while mapped to midfield due to hold-up overcrowding, the strong trainer angle (1/17 T14) and recent record are compelling.

runners_data.name: Penzance
runners_data.note: Outstanding second-season record of five good-ground placed efforts at 16f-18f (0W5P) for the same Hanlon yard — consistent and stays the trip well, but needs to convert; tongue-and-cheek combo and clear good-ground affinity make this a natural place candidate in any shape.

runners_data.name: Party President
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie removed this season and a second at 16f on soft marks a return to form; Leahy yard (0/1 T14) is quiet and the hold-up style is genuine, though the horse has been placed well off the pace rather than winning from it — mapped to midfield from the true rear.

runners_data.name: Coolboy Christy
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell five-year-old wearing a hood who has shown consistent mid-division finishes (4-5 range) without threatening in recent handicaps; blinkered here for the first time, and the lack of a win over this longer 2m½f journey is a concern.

runners_data.name: Imperial Miss
runners_data.note: 231-day absence for Thomas Gibney's string (0/6 T14) is a significant fitness concern; a second over 22f on good ground last season offers distance credentials but the long layoff and modest recent form make it hard to assess current wellbeing.

runners_data.name: Space Warrior
runners_data.note: Thomas Mullins five-year-old who placed at 17f on good ground but also unseated and pulled up in recent starts — inconsistency and a horse that has only once beaten half the field in five efforts on similar going makes this a speculative hold-up candidate at best.

runners_data.name: Torque De Lune
runners_data.note: Hanlon six-year-old with three recent falls/unseats/unknowns in the form string (F, U, ?) and a career record on good ground that reads 0W1P from six; mapped to midfield from the rear, and jumping safety is the principal concern in an 18-runner field.

runners_data.name: Dream Shaper
runners_data.note: Won over 19f good ground (1/19) most recently and placed over 20f — the best stamina profile in the field; trainer Madden (1/2 T14) is live, tongue-tie applied, and while a genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield by necessity, the combination of trip form and recent winning run makes this a strong late-race threat.

races.paceDynamic: Cloonainra is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and should secure an uncontested lead from the outset, setting a sustainable gallop on good ground over 2m½f at Galway. Behind him, the field is dominated by hold-up horses — Timurshah, My Trump Card, Tassarolo, Playtime and a raft of others — who will settle in behind and look to close late off what is likely to be a measured pace. The field carries significantly more hold-up and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate naturally; Bannow Blaze, Barrys Spirit, Castleheath, Penzance and Mo Ghille Mar are genuine closer/prominent types who will be crowding the rear-to-middle, and none can truly get their natural position in this traffic. Cloonainra dictates terms, the pace will not be excessive, and the race will set up for horses who can travel prominently or have a high cruising speed to pick off a front-runner who has had things his own way — the tactical verdict favours prominent-to-midfield runners with strong good-ground form who can close efficiently without needing a breakneck gallop to bring them into play.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cloonainra Controls, Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If Cloonainra bowls along at a fair but unhurried clip and the large field fails to produce a rival who challenges him early, setting up a one-pace finish.
scenarios.body: Cloonainra finds his rhythm and stretches the field into a strung-out line, but with no pressure he doesn't empty and a wall of closers converges in the straight; horses with strong good-ground form and the ability to pick up from mid-division are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Stayers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely slow, bunching the field and forcing a kick from the home turn that exposes stamina over this 2m½f trip.
scenarios.body: A compressed pack races into the straight with little daylight and the race becomes a test of staying power and jumping fluency rather than pace; horses with proven stamina at this trip and class on good ground are best placed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Front Two Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the tight 18-runner field produces scrimmaging mid-race, leaving Cloonainra and any horse that follows him through in clean air.
scenarios.body: Horses trapped in the midfield melee lose momentum and ground at crucial points, gifting a clear advantage to the early leader and whoever tracks him; a prominent-running profile with course and good-ground form is essential.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Flyers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If a stronger-than-expected pace develops — perhaps from a prominent-type pressing Cloonainra — leaving the field strung out and genuine hold-up horses finishing fastest.
scenarios.body: A true end-to-end gallop would exhaust the front-runners and compress finishing times at the back, rewarding the deepest closers who can find clear runs in a big field; good-ground speed figures matter most here.

watchPoints.text: Timurshah arrives off three consecutive wins on good ground including at this trip and course conditions — watch whether Conor Smithers can navigate the 18-runner field cleanly from the hold-up position, because a clear run could see him accelerate to a fourth consecutive victory.

Dream Shaper won over 19f good ground just nine days ago and Madden has a live 14-day record (1/2); if Brian Barry can get a clear run in the straight this staying profile could swoop late having settled at the rear of a sustainable pace.

Cloonainra must be respected as the sole confirmed pace-setter — if he bowls along unchallenged he could prove very difficult to reel in on good ground, and any horse that secures second or third position directly behind him from the start holds a significant tactical advantage.

Mo Ghille Mar and Penzance double up for John Joseph Hanlon (1/17 T14) — watch which one the yard saddles as the main hope; Penzance's extraordinary placed consistency and Mo Ghille Mar's recent winning form make either a threat if the stable has a lead runner.

Wahraan runs back just four days after winning over 18f good ground — the short turnaround is unusual and worth monitoring in pre-race markets; if fit and well, the proven staying form and tongue-tie give the horse a live each-way profile, but any signs of stiffness in the betting should be heeded.

races.name: Kenny Galway Peugeot Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Sir Allen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse on Good going where he has placed three times in five runs; the 12-day turnaround is fine, and a 7-year-old for Andrew Slattery ridden by the claiming apprentice Sam Coen, he needs the race to truly be run to get competitive from the rear of such a large field.

runners_data.name: Burning Ability
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who ran just yesterday — the 1-day turnaround is a significant fitness flag — but has a strong record on Good ground (won over 20f) and Noel Christopher McCarthy's runner could get a perfect sit in behind the front pair if he lines up.

runners_data.name: High Court Cave
runners_data.note: Prominent type carrying hood for Noel Kelly; 35-day break since last run and only one win from ten Good-ground starts, but he has finished second on this course and trip combination before, making the experience relevant.

runners_data.name: Mr Master Mac
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer with a remarkable 5-from-5 record on Good going including two wins; the 49-day absence is the only query, but a 7lb claimer on a five-year-old for Mark Fahey who saves weight looks an interesting combination in what should be a truly run race.

runners_data.name: Pinot Rouge
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has headgear (p) on and has placed twice on Good ground over distances matching today's trip; the 50-day break is a concern, and his two softest-ground runs produced his worst finishes, suggesting Good suits him.

runners_data.name: Rocky's Howya
runners_data.note: The senior front-runner of the field at ten years old, with a tongue-tie and a genuine love of Good ground (three wins); trainer-ridden by Mr D L Queally, he will go forward immediately and set the primary pace throughout.

runners_data.name: Fou De Toi
runners_data.note: Paul Townend — Mullins' stable jockey — takes the ride on this lightly-raced five-year-old who has only one Good-ground start in five, finishing second; the market will tell the story but the booking is as strong as it gets in this race.

runners_data.name: Reiki Revolution
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a hood (ht) who has had two unseating incidents recently (UU in form); his Good-ground record is limited to 2 from 14 relevant runs, and Gavin Cromwell has had no runners in the last 30 days, making his readiness uncertain.

runners_data.name: Stormbreaker
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer whose last five runs on soft/yielding ground produced modest results; today's Good ground is a clear improvement on his recent conditions, though a 21-day break and modest finishing positions in similar company don't inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Warriors Wood
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up horse for Andrew McNamara, ran just 2 days ago yet posts an excellent Good-ground record of 3 wins and 6 places from 13 runs; the short turnaround is noteworthy but the form profile on this surface is arguably the best in the field.

runners_data.name: Elusive Ogie
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Eoin McCarthy, stablemate of Burning Ability; his last 11 Good-ground runs produced only 1 win and 3 places and recent form shows a fall (F), leaving his confidence and current form both questionable.

runners_data.name: Moonovercloon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying a visor, ran 2 days ago, and has a concerning record — 0 wins from 15 Good-ground starts; his last outing produced a pulled-up, and at nine years old this represents a very steep ask even if he meets the race in a good place.

runners_data.name: Forceonmyown
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning from 110 days off for Gordon Elliott, who has had 4 runners in 14 days; the absence is the defining factor here and his eight relevant Good-ground runs produced no wins or places, making a return to form on debut back hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Tullyveery Lad
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a bite (b) in headgear who has run all 15 Good-ground starts at this course and distance combination — 2 wins and 6 places is a striking statistic; the second last time out (24f, Good) suggests he remains competitive at the top of handicap.

runners_data.name: Mento
runners_data.note: The younger of the two confirmed front-runners at just four years old; won last time on Good over 19f and will want to bowl along in front, though stepping up markedly in trip to 3m½f for the first time introduces real stamina doubt, especially against more seasoned opponents.

runners_data.name: Beggars Rock
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a tongue-tie and visor (tv) returning after 78 days off; placed three times on Good ground in six attempts, including over 26f suggesting stamina is there, but the absence and the size of the field both work against him significantly.

runners_data.name: Caher Roes Den
runners_data.note: Prominent type for Willie Mullins partnered by Danny Mullins; only one placing on Good going in seven relevant runs, though the trainer's 10-from-47 14-day strike rate is strong and this runner brings soft-ground form to a Good-ground test that may not suit.

runners_data.name: Adaliz
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a bite (b) in headgear for Henry De Bromhead; won on Good going (24f) three runs back and has placed on Good before, though two of his last three results are 9th and 10th, raising questions about current form.

runners_data.name: Sallap
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer — noted as fading in the finish — who has won three times on Good going including twice over 22f; pushed into a mapped midfield position because of the surplus of hold-up types, meaning his natural closer's run may be compromised in this shape.

runners_data.name: Justatan
runners_data.note: Real hold-up horse for Emmet Mullins with a tongue-tie and hood (tp) who placed 3rd on Good over 26f last time — the most relevant piece of recent form; mapped to midfield because of field congestion, which is the key discount on his chance today.

runners_data.name: Wild Mandate
runners_data.note: A genuinely prominent-natured runner for Mark McNiff who has won on Good over 26f; because there are more prominent types than positions available, he is unlikely to get his favoured spot, and the reserve jockey booking adds further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Fair Damsel
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up type mapped into midfield due to field congestion; ten recent Good-ground runs produced just 1 win and 2 places, and the reserve jockey booking on a horse already racing out of its preferred position makes this a difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Pat Coyne
runners_data.note: At 12 years old the oldest horse in the race and a natural hold-up performer; mapped away from his true rear position because of the surplus of closers, and a 70-day layoff combined with the advanced age and reserve jockey compound the challenges considerably.

races.paceDynamic: Rocky's Howya and Mento are the two confirmed front-runners in a 23-runner field, and both are likely to press forward from the off over this 3m½f trip, creating a genuinely contested gallop rather than a soft-pedalled early pace. Rocky's Howya has won three times on Good ground and clearly relishes these conditions, while Mento, a four-year-old who led and won last time out, will not want to be buried in a large field and will challenge for the front. The resulting honest, competitive gallop over an extended trip on Good ground at Galway — a track that already tests stamina through its undulations — should stretch the field significantly in the final half-mile and bring staying hold-up horses into play from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours genuine stayers who can be produced with a late run, but the field contains a surplus of both prominent and hold-up types: Wild Mandate, Sallap, Justatan, Fair Damsel and Pat Coyne cannot all secure their natural positions, with Burning Ability, High Court Cave and Fou De Toi the prominent types most likely to actually hold their forward berths given their profile and connections.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If Rocky's Howya and Mento cut out a genuine gallop and the race is truly run, setting up a stamina test that favours horses coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn each other and the field up the Galway straight, leaving the race wide open for horses who have been produced patiently; the final climb at Galway rewards those with a full tank. True hold-up horses with good Good-ground form are the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Rocky's Howya or Mento manages to establish a comfortable lead and the early pace is less brutal than anticipated, allowing the leader to dictate terms.
scenarios.body: A controlled gallop from the front means the leader conserves enough to sustain the effort all the way to the line; Rocky's Howya's three wins on Good ground and trainer-rider combination make him particularly dangerous in this shape. The prominent horses tucked in behind also benefit as they get a soft lead rather than a lung-bursting test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Thrive
scenarios.trigger: If the front pair set a strong but sustainable gallop and the race sorts itself out in the straight, rewarding horses who tracked the pace efficiently rather than coming from furthest back.
scenarios.body: Horses racing prominently but not on the lead avoid the early scrapping while still travelling into a good position; the Good going at Galway allows them to pick up smoothly when asked. Burning Ability and Fou De Toi both have the profile for this — Mullins' runner carries significant market interest and Townend is a key booking.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Fail to Land
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race or the front two are allowed to coast, and the late-running hold-up brigade cannot make sufficient ground on the run-in.
scenarios.body: In this shape those held up in the rear — including those redistributed from their natural position — simply face too much ground to make up against a controlling front runner on Good ground; winners are found closer to the pace rather than from the back. Caher Roes Den and Adaliz, both prominent types with Good-ground form, are the profile this shape helps.

watchPoints.text: Rocky's Howya and Mento will dispute the front from the start — watch if either rider concedes or whether they force a true pace; if Mento fades on the extended trip, Rocky's Howya could lead unchallenged and dramatically change the race shape.

Warriors Wood ran just two days ago and the rapid turnaround could compromise his finishing effort; watch his behaviour in the parade ring and whether Kevin Healy (7) settles him before committing to a hold-up ride in a big field.

Sallap and Justatan are genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on this map — watch whether either rider elects to drop back to their natural position regardless, which would mean they are racing from further back than the map suggests and need an even stronger pace to succeed.

Fou De Toi's fitness is unknown following a 30-day break, but the Paul Townend booking in a Mullins-trained runner is one of the strongest market signals in this race; watch the market move at 30 minutes to post as a key form indicator.

Mento is only four years old and today's 3m½f is comfortably the furthest he has run — watch whether Josh Williamson tries to control the pace or allows Rocky's Howya to dominate, as the stamina question for the younger horse is the single biggest variable in how this race unfolds.

races.name: Kinlay Hostel Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Soldante
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with an excellent three-from-three placing record on Good, trained by Ciaran Murphy whose yard is in decent nick (1/15 in 14 days); only 6 days since last run which is worth monitoring, but the 2m6f trip and surface are ideal for his profile.

runners_data.name: Ira Hayes
runners_data.note: Veteran of 22-28f races on Good ground with a win at 22f in that going, though 56 days off adds a fitness query; John McConnell's yard is cold (0/27 in 14 days) and the headgear note (visor) suggests a horse that needs things to go right tactically.

runners_data.name: Journey So Far
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in finishes, which is a serious concern over 2m6½f with a hot pace; won last time at 22f on Good but the fade warning and 65-day absence make this a risky proposition despite Donoghue's booking.

runners_data.name: Kings Jet
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a scattered recent record including pulled-up and unseated finishes, but has a course win and Good-ground experience; the amateur rider (7lb claim) is a notable negative in a race of this size and class.

runners_data.name: Lawful Ruler
runners_data.note: One of only two confirmed front-runners so will have his position, though recent form includes a pull-up and his last win was on Good at 24f — the amateur rider is a concern over this trip with Gorthill alongside him.

runners_data.name: Sammy Smart
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominent type whose recent form includes a pull-up and an unseated, though four of his last five sim-going runs were placed; Thomas Gibney's yard is quiet and the age is a flag in a race this competitive.

runners_data.name: Golden Temple
runners_data.note: Lightly raced six-year-old for Noel Meade, whose yard is active (3/17 in 14 days), with a win at 20f on Good and second most recently; only 4 days since last run is tight but the tongue-strap use and improving profile make him a shape beneficiary if the pace plays into hold-up hands.

runners_data.name: Prince Palace
runners_data.note: Zero wins and zero places from seven sim-going runs tells a stark story; headgear (blinkers) and two P J Rothwell runners in the race split the trainer's attention, and the horse's Good-ground record over this distance offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Inchidaly Copper
runners_data.note: Phenomenal sim-going record — 14 from 15 on Good ground with four wins — and consistently placed (3-3-3-1-3 in recent history); the yard is cold (0 runners in 14 days) but the surface and trip are a bulls-eye fit for this ten-year-old prominent type.

runners_data.name: Le Grand Vert
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with proven 26f form on Good including two of his last four at that trip, though two of five recent runs are pulled-ups; tongue-strap suggests wind issues but a second and a win in similar conditions keep him relevant if he completes.

runners_data.name: Drop A Threat
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins sends this seven-year-old from a powerful yard (10/47 in 14 days) with Danny Mullins aboard, but form reads 4-0-P-5-6 and sim-going returns show zero wins and zero places from 7 Good-ground outings — the numbers don't flatter the profile.

runners_data.name: Noble Talent
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose last five runs contain four pulled-ups or pulled equivalents; mapped to midfield due to redistribution in this crowded field, but even that more forward position won't compensate for a form line that reads poorly on Good ground at any trip.

runners_data.name: Riggs
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old hold-up specialist with a 15-from-15 sim-going record (2W, 3P) showing he handles Good, but recent form is 6-8-P-8-P; shuffled forward on the map because the rear is oversubscribed, meaning he likely won't get his true rhythmical position and his chance is discounted accordingly.

runners_data.name: Jukebox Johnny
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Henry De Bromhead (5/39 in 14 days) with Darragh O'Keeffe riding, finishing second most recently over 22f on Good; tongue-strap and pad headgear combination and only 3-from-8 sim-going returns suggest he is inconsistent but the jockey/trainer combination keeps him in the picture.

runners_data.name: Gorthill
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner alongside Lawful Ruler; a 10-year-old with a string of placed finishes at 29f on Good, so the trip suits, but recent form is P-U-P-5-P and the amateur rider adds risk — more likely to be the hare than the hound.

runners_data.name: Saunton Surf
runners_data.note: Won his last two (24f Good, 20f Good) with a prominent style, and the form line is sharp; the paddock headgear (hood) is new but the trainer's yard is quiet, and 50 days since last run needs to be factored in for a horse operating at this level.

runners_data.name: Smallcraftwarning
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with a 14-from-15 sim-going record entirely on Good and seven places from his last 15, but none have converted to wins; placed well into the map because hold-up slots are exhausted, so his natural closing style is compromised and the STYLE_FIT discount applies.

runners_data.name: Mistyburn
runners_data.note: Young six-year-old for P J Rothwell (yard running two) who won at 24f on Good and placed at 24f subsequently — form is more credible than his OR of 87 suggests; a true hold-up horse pushed to a midfield map position, so his late-run potential depends on a strong pace collapse that opens ground in the straight.

races.paceDynamic: Lawful Ruler and Gorthill are the confirmed front-runners and will push for the lead from the off, creating a genuinely contested gallop over 2m6½f on Good ground — neither is likely to yield, so the pace will be honest rather than manufactured. With 18 runners across a stiff Galway staying trip, that sustained pressure will string the field out and test resolution from three out, likely causing the lead to crack in the home straight. Prominent racers who can travel economically close to the pace — Soldante, Ira Hayes, Inchidaly Copper and Jukebox Johnny — are best placed to inherit momentum when the front two fade, while deep hold-up horses must generate significant ground from off the bridle. The field contains more genuine hold-up types than the map can show at the rear — Noble Talent, Riggs, Smallcraftwarning and Mistyburn are true closers shuffled into midfield on the map, and Riggs and Noble Talent are the least likely to recover their preferred ground in an 18-runner chasing field; the race shape firmly favours prominent racers with proven Good-ground form at this trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Two Fold, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Lawful Ruler and Gorthill set a pressured gallop and capitulate from three out, handing the race to the prominent pack.
scenarios.body: The contested early pace burns out the front-runners over the stiff 2m6½f trip, leaving prominent horses who have tracked efficiently in prime position entering the straight. Inchidaly Copper and Soldante profile perfectly here — both have the Good-ground form and the positional awareness to pounce when the lead collapses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lawful Ruler Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Lawful Ruler dictates a controlled gallop, shaking off Gorthill mid-race and building an unassailable lead.
scenarios.body: A junior amateur partnership with Lawful Ruler adds uncertainty, but if Paul Stafford's gelding gets his rhythm and Gorthill fades early, a solo lead at a comfortable clip makes this a thorough stayer's race. Prominent types who get the trip strongly — Saunton Surf and Le Grand Vert — offer the best chance of running him down if he gets first run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Big-Field Traffic, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is sufficiently fierce that it creates a true test of stamina and bunching in the home straight opens a late lane.
scenarios.body: An 18-runner field over fences generates interference and gaps that can occasionally open for horses launching from well off the pace in the final half mile. Golden Temple and Journey So Far have the class and Good-ground credentials to pick off tiring rivals, though both need everything to fall right in a field this size.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Carnage Thins Field, Survivor Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the hot gallop and Galway's demanding fences cause a high attrition rate, leaving a survivor to coast home.
scenarios.body: With 18 runners over fences at pace, jumping errors and fallers are a real possibility, and a horse who jumps economically at a steady second rhythm through the chaos can benefit regardless of style. Kings Jet and Sammy Smart — both experienced jumpers with previous completions at the course — could capitalise if the race falls apart ahead of them.

watchPoints.text: Watch Gorthill's jumping from the first fence — a 10-year-old front-runner with a string of recent non-completions (P-U-P) could cause serious interference if he makes a jumping error while disputing the lead in an 18-runner field.

Lawful Ruler and Gorthill will clash for the lead immediately; if neither concedes, a frantic early gallop risks burning out both horses and creating a dangerous vacuum from the third last — track Lawful Ruler's rhythm through the first mile.

Inchidaly Copper's trainer Alexander Ott has zero runners in the last 14 days and the yard form is cold — despite the horse's exceptional sim-going record, confirm paddock condition and market support before elevating its chance.

Drop A Threat carries the weight of a top yard (Mullins/D Mullins) but has zero wins and zero places from seven Good-ground outings in similar conditions — stable confidence will be visible in early market moves and is worth tracking.

With four confirmed or probable redistributed hold-up horses (Noble Talent, Riggs, Smallcraftwarning, Mistyburn) all racing further forward than their nature dictates, monitor whether any of them are taken wide early to manufacture a clear passage, which could further stretch the field and alter sectional dynamics.

races.name: Lord Hemphill Memorial Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Blood Destiny
runners_data.note: Mullins/Townend at 10/47 over 14 days is a powerful combination; confirmed front-runner who won on similar going 62 days ago, and the headgear (hg:t) supports a bold front-running display, though his recent P125-2 form suggests he can be headed under pressure.

runners_data.name: Coming Up Easy
runners_data.note: Three wins from four completions on Good or similar going is an outstanding stat for De Bromhead's 8-year-old; races prominently and has the class (OR 140) to sit just off a contested pace and pounce, though 114 days off the track is the chief query.

runners_data.name: Runcok
runners_data.note: A genuine lead horse by style whose recent form (F174-6) shows a tendency to fade after dominating early — likely to press Blood Destiny hard but vulnerable from the fourth-last onwards; McConnell's yard is 0/27 over 14 days, adding an in-form concern.

runners_data.name: Le Nez Creux
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's 5-year-old carries all five recent runs on Heavy ground and has zero recorded Good-ground appearances — an important unknown despite consistent placing form; races prominently, which suits the anticipated race shape, but the going is a genuine concern.

runners_data.name: Path d'Oroux
runners_data.note: Ran just one day ago (LR:1d), which is a major flag — a horse running back on consecutive days in a competitive handicap chase deserves significant scepticism regardless of hold-up style; form 4950-0 on Good suggests he is not in peak form.

runners_data.name: The Banger Doyle
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with seven placed efforts from fifteen Good-ground runs; John Queally's yard is 0/1 over 14 days and the 10-year-old needs a true pace test to bring his staying-on style into play, which this race should provide.

runners_data.name: Drumgill
runners_data.note: A pure hold-up type (H) yet to win on Good going from seven attempts — the sim-going record (0W0P) is damning for this surface; amateur claimer Kenneally takes a 5lb claim but this horse requires soft conditions to be at his best.

runners_data.name: Lisleigh Lad
runners_data.note: Returned to winning form 30 days ago over 20f on Good — the most recent relevant form in the field on similar going and distance; races prominently (style=P), which is the profile this pace scenario rewards most, and Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim helps at the weights.

runners_data.name: War Correspondent
runners_data.note: Fourteen of fifteen runs on Good going shows an adaptable, reliable horse who just keeps hitting the frame (1W6P); genuine hold-up racer who needs a strong pace to close into — this contest provides it, though Paddy Hanlon (5) is a relatively inexperienced claimer.

runners_data.name: Itsalladream
runners_data.note: Paul John Gilligan's 7-year-old is a natural hold-up horse whose four consecutive fifth-place finishes on Good ground suggest it stays well but struggles to win; pushed into a midfield mapping by the volume of rear-end types in this field, meaning it is unlikely to find its natural rhythm.

runners_data.name: Watch The Weather
runners_data.note: Strong Good-ground record (12/15 runs) is a positive, but a 10-year-old rated 121 whose most recent form includes an 8 and a 5 on similar going is not progressing; this horse's instinct is to settle and close, yet the crowded hold-up group means it cannot easily find open ground early.

runners_data.name: Bythesametoken
runners_data.note: At 12 years old and 114 days off the track, Ross O'Sullivan's veteran faces significant fitness questions returning from a break; a true hold-up horse by nature whose best form has come on Soft going (1W on Soft, 0W on Good), making the Good surface another meaningful negative.

races.paceDynamic: Blood Destiny and Runcok are both confirmed front-runners and will fight for the lead from the off, creating a genuinely contested gallop on Good ground over 2m2f at Galway — neither is likely to yield without a battle. That contested early pace sets up a demanding race shape where the leaders are likely to be pressed throughout, burning enough fuel to crack before the final fences. This scenario structurally favours horses capable of travelling prominently just off the pace — Coming Up Easy, Le Nez Creux and Lisleigh Lad are ideally positioned to exploit any weakness in the front two — or resolute hold-up types who can produce a sustained late run into a race run at honest tempo. The verdict is clear: prominent racers who travel within themselves behind the front-running duel are the primary beneficiaries; true hold-up types may also stay on past spent pace-setters, but the race shape most rewards the prominent profile. Itsalladream, Watch The Weather and Bythesametoken are genuine hold-up horses who have been mapped to midfield because the rear end of this field is crowded — Blood Destiny and Runcok, backed up by the naturally prominent Coming Up Easy and Le Nez Creux, are those best placed to dictate their preferred positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Blood Destiny and Runcok fight for the lead and burn each other out, handing the race to a tracking horse in the straight.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a genuine gallop that taxes both of them over the final fences, allowing a prominent stalker to cruise up and collar them late; Coming Up Easy's strong form on Good ground and Le Nez Creux's consistent placing profile make them ideal hunters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Duel
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners — most likely Blood Destiny — controls the tempo sufficiently to avoid being burned off and quickens clear at the last.
scenarios.body: Blood Destiny, trained by Mullins with Townend aboard and a recent win on similar going, has the class edge and may dictate a pace that suits himself after shaking off Runcok; Runcok's tendency to fade (form 174-6) makes Blood Destiny the more likely survivor if the contest resolves early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace truly collapses the front-runners and leaves a genuine gap for closers sweeping through beaten horses in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The Banger Doyle and War Correspondent have the staying-on profile to benefit from a strong pace that has exhausted the leaders, both showing repeated good ground placed form at this sort of trip; however, Itsalladream, Watch The Weather and Bythesametoken — though natural hold-up types — face the complication of having been pushed further forward than ideal by the crowded rear of this field, slightly diluting their true closing advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Moderate, Midfield Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If early pace proves less severe than expected and Runcok or Blood Destiny settles, creating a slowly-run race where midfield types accelerate from an unpredictable point.
scenarios.body: A moderated tempo compresses the field and turns it into a jumping test decided late, where Lisleigh Lad's recent win and strong Good-ground record give him a consistent platform; War Correspondent's near-miss form profile and proven ability on Good going also suit a race that rewards accurate jumping over raw stamina.

watchPoints.text: Blood Destiny and Runcok — watch whether one attempts to dominate from the front immediately; if Runcok fires early and Blood Destiny matches him stride for stride, the pace will be punishing and both may be beaten horses from the third-last.

Path d'Oroux ran only one day ago and connections need to be watched in the market — if he drifts sharply, the one-day turnaround has taken a physical toll and he becomes a significant risk to backers and a potential danger at fences.

Le Nez Creux has never been recorded running on Good ground — all five career runs are on Heavy — watch how he moves in the paddock and through the early fences; if he is not comfortable on the firmer surface, his prominent style could see him cramp up before the finish.

Lisleigh Lad — watch his jumping accuracy from an early stage; he races prominently and has winning form at this trip on Good, but if he makes a jumping error in a strongly-run race, recovery from a prominent position is very difficult over fences.

Coming Up Easy — watch the market closely given 114 days off the course; if De Bromhead's yard has him tuned up and the market shortens, the layoff concern diminishes and his Good-ground winning profile becomes the standout angle in the race.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Ahonoora Handicap

runners_data.name: Jagged Edge
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong good-ground form (2W3P in similar conditions), in cracking recent form and last won over 8f — dropping to 7f here is a slight query but should be fine; Jack Kearney's 3lb claim is useful in a competitive handicap.|

runners_data.name: Vafortino
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up specialist who has failed to win in 15 good-ground starts and hasn't run for 45 days; his record at the trip is poor and he needs things to fall perfectly from the rear in a big field.|

runners_data.name: Dorset
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, trained by Aidan O'Brien and ridden by Wayne Lordan — ran just four days ago which is worth monitoring for freshness, but his role as uncontested pace-setter is the dominant tactical factor in this race.|

runners_data.name: Dunum
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who showed a win over 8f on good ground and has the profile to track Dorset; eight years old and form has been patchy recently, but the trainer has a 0/6 14-day strike rate which tempers confidence.|

runners_data.name: Gleneagle Bay
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse ridden by the in-form Dylan Browne McMonagle — ran just five days ago, wears a hood (hg:p), and his best recent run (1st) came over 7f on good ground, suggesting the conditions and trip fit well.|

runners_data.name: Orandi
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type in running style, shifted into midfield on the map due to field size; his good-ground record at the trip is modest and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) suggests he won't get his ideal racing position, which tempers his chance.|

runners_data.name: Unique Journey
runners_data.note: Prominent racer stepping up in trip sharply from 6f sprints where all five career wins have come; 71 days off and untested at 7f are meaningful questions, though good-ground form is solid.|

runners_data.name: Lord Massusus
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer but without a win from 10 good-ground starts — placed form is non-existent on good going and the trend of finishing mid-division makes him difficult to recommend at this level.|

runners_data.name: Bold Style
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot by field congestion (STYLE_FIT 0.92); his three places on good ground show he has ability, but racing out of role reduces his chance of delivering in the expected race shape.|

runners_data.name: City House
runners_data.note: Genuine closer whose natural position at the rear is unavailable in this crowded field — placed four times on good ground but the redistribution into midfield (STYLE_FIT 0.93) means he must produce his best from an uncharacteristic berth.|

runners_data.name: Dark Ace
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best form was on artificial surfaces (two wins on Standard); only 4 runs on good going with no wins suggests the conditions are not ideal, and he arrives 15 days off.|

runners_data.name: Far From Dandy
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer who has finished second twice recently over 8f on good/soft ground — dropping to 7f on good going is potentially sharper than ideal, but his finishing kick could be relevant if the pace builds from three furlongs out.|

runners_data.name: Dos Mukasan
runners_data.note: True closer who sits out of position as a redistribution in midfield (STYLE_FIT 0.92); 91 days off is a major flag, and his one win on good going came over a longer trip — getting the 7f on a first run back is a big ask.|

runners_data.name: Pierre Royal
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has been in outstanding form (2W4P in 6 good-ground starts); won over 8f recently and all five recorded runs in these conditions have yielded a place — travelling up close to Dorset suits his profile ideally.|

runners_data.name: Genuine Article
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse mapped to midfield by necessity (STYLE_FIT 0.93); no wins on good ground and a recent run over 16f signals a horse coming back in trip sharply — style mismatch and form concerns both work against him.|

runners_data.name: Lir Speciale
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent/midfield performer with four places in his last five on good ground at 7-8f; trained in Britain by Brian Ellison (0/29 14-day), and Chris Hayes is a useful booking — finished second over 7f on good ground twice recently.|

runners_data.name: Greydreambeliever
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse shown in midfield due to field size (STYLE_FIT 0.92); Joseph O'Brien's yard is in flying form (15/78 14-day) and two recent second-place finishes at 7f on good/soft ground show course-relevant ability — trainer form is the strongest case here.|

runners_data.name: Glory To Be
runners_data.note: Prominent racer without a listed jockey, which is a flag in an 18-runner field — won over 7f on good ground and has placed five times in that profile, but the booking situation needs monitoring before the race.|

races.paceDynamic: Dorset is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner flat handicap at Galway and, critically, faces no meaningful pace pressure — with no rival willing or able to dispute the lead, Wayne Lordan can dictate a controlled, honest gallop across the seven furlongs. Jagged Edge and Dunum will look to press from prominent positions, with Pierre Royal and Lir Speciale also likely to take closer order, creating a strung-out but not scorching tempo that keeps the race honest without turning it into a sprint test. The field holds significantly more hold-up and prominent horses than the race shape can accommodate naturally — City House, Bold Style, Dos Mukasan, and Genuine Article are genuine closers who will be shuffled back into midfield rather than finding their natural rear-dropping berth, meaning the late surge will be crowded and competitive. With one front-runner controlling a sustainable gallop on good turf over seven furlongs, this race shape heavily favours horses who can travel prominently in the slipstream of Dorset and produce their effort from the two-furlong pole — prominent racers who handle good ground and get the trip are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dorset Dictates, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Dorset sets a controlled, uncontested gallop and prominent stalkers time their challenge from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Dorset leads at a measured pace, with Jagged Edge and Pierre Royal travelling in his wake and launching sustained challenges in the straight; on good ground over seven furlongs, horses who race in the first four early have a clear positional edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Hotts Up, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If early momentum quickens unexpectedly and prominent horses are caught flat-footed inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected gallop stretches the field and leaves front-end horses vulnerable late, allowing genuine hold-up types who find clear runs to reel in the leaders; Gleneagle Bay and Far From Dandy are among those with the profile to benefit if a run materialises.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Scores Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Dorset sets a modest enough tempo that rivals cannot sustain momentum to reel him in over seven furlongs.
scenarios.body: With no challenger willing to force the pace, Lordan nurses Dorset through fractions and kicks clear before rivals in mid-division can organise their challenges; horses camped too far back in a large field on a straight seven furlongs struggle to make up the ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Cavalry Charge
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a stop-start pace that compresses the field and triggers a mass challenge from the three-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Redistributed closers like Bold Style and City House, unable to get their natural position at the rear, find themselves travelling kindly in midfield and emerge late into a bunched finish; the winner comes from a mass surge rather than a positional edge.

watchPoints.text: Dorset (Lordan/A P O'Brien) ran just four days ago — watch for any market drift or veterinary inspection before the race, as fatigue from a very recent run could compromise his ability to control the pace.

Pierre Royal has placed in all six good-ground starts and travels close to the pace naturally — watch whether Adam Caffrey slots him directly behind Dorset in the opening two furlongs, as that position is the key to his challenge.

Gleneagle Bay (Dylan Browne McMonagle) is the most dangerous hold-up threat if the pace quickens — watch his position at the two-furlong pole; if he has a run, he has the form at the trip and going to come from midfield to win.

The redistribution of five genuine closers (City House, Bold Style, Dos Mukasan, Genuine Article, Greydreambeliever) into midfield creates significant traffic risk in the straight — watch for a congested final two furlongs where runners without a clear passage will be severely disadvantaged.

Glory To Be and Greydreambeliever both lack confirmed jockey bookings — confirm riders before the off, as a top-tier late booking on either could signal stable confidence that the market has not yet priced in.

races.name: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden

runners_data.name: Dakota Jack
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has experience over this exact 7f Good ground combination (2 from 2 in similar going); Robert Whearty takes the ride for a yard in decent 14-day form, and six days since last run is a positive freshness angle — well placed to stalk Star Glory and produce a clean turn of foot.

runners_data.name: Scotty Cameron
runners_data.note: Finished last on sole start over 6f on Good ground; Leigh Roche rides for Coleman's yard but the fading-in-finish flag is a real concern, and as a genuine hold-up type this horse needs the pace to collapse in order to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Hypiradon
runners_data.note: Coleman's yard runs this horse alongside Scotty Cameron; its true style is hold-up but congestion at the rear means it is unlikely to secure that position — shown in midfield on the map — and it carries a 0.90 style-fit discount that should temper confidence in any scenario requiring it to race from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Miss Cornelia
runners_data.note: Lightly raced filly who ran sixth over this exact 7f Good course combination; Gary Carroll is a sharp tactical jockey and Joseph Murphy's yard has a runner in the last seven days, but the unknown style (U) means she is a wildcard whose positional play cannot be predicted with confidence.

runners_data.name: Gabby Hayes
runners_data.note: Debuting for Noel Meade — the stable has sent out three winners in 17 days — but going is listed UNKNOWN and she is unraced, making her an entirely speculative runner; Siobhan Rutledge takes the ride and the filly could be anything, placing her as an each-way wildcard in any scenario that becomes a raw-speed dash.

runners_data.name: Oristown Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with form showing a distant fourth over 7f on Soft and a poor thirteenth on Good over 6f; Rory Mulligan takes the 5lb claim and 44 days since last run is a query, though the step back to easier ground is marginally encouraging for this rider-trainer combination with limited recent strike rate.

runners_data.name: Whosinterviewinwho
runners_data.note: Held-up runner trained and ridden by Andrew Slattery; finished fifth over 6f Good and seventh over 8f Good, suggesting the 7f trip is potentially ideal, but the yard's 2-from-31 in 14 days is a cold strike rate and this horse needs a true gallop to deliver its best.

runners_data.name: Seaxburh
runners_data.note: The most exposed runner in the field with four starts showing two seconds over 7f Good — directly relevant form — for O'Brien's powerful yard with Dylan Browne McMonagle, arguably the standout jockey booking here; prominent style with headgear flagged and consistent good-ground form makes her a clear shape beneficiary.

runners_data.name: Star Glory
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who holds the tactical keys but carries a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 suggesting the map position is not its most natural role; Chris Hayes for Noel Meade is a strong booking and the horse placed second over 7f Good, though it will need to set the right tempo to maximise its own chance rather than simply set it up for the prominent trackers.

runners_data.name: Someday Somewhere
runners_data.note: Ran third over 6f Good on sole start for Stephen Thorne's yard (zero wins in 10 from 14 days) with W J Lee in the plate; unknown style but lightly raced and the step up to 7f is unproven — could benefit in a slow-run scramble but evidence is thin and the trainer's recent form offers little confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Star Glory is the lone confirmed front-runner and, on good ground over 7f at Galway, is likely to dictate at a sustainable tempo without any genuine challenger pressing from the front. Dakota Jack and Seaxburh are the principal prominent types who will track in the first two or three lengths, giving the race a controlled shape rather than a truly run gallop. The hold-up contingent — Scotty Cameron, Hypiradon, Oristown Boy, and Whosinterviewinwho — will be ridden from off the pace, but with Hypiradon redistributed to midfield on the map due to congestion at the rear, the true hold-up group is denser than the diagram shows, and Hypiradon is unlikely to find its natural position. This controlled, single-pace shape on a flat track over 7f strongly favours horses who can travel prominently, quicken into the straight, and sustain their effort — tracking runners with a finishing kick hold the clearest tactical advantage, while genuine deep closers face an uphill task against a pace that will not truly collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Star Glory sets a sustainable pace unchallenged and the race is won by a horse tracking in second or third.
scenarios.body: Star Glory rolls along at a fair but uncontested tempo, leaving the leading prominent and prominent-tracking types to coast within striking range before kicking decisively into the home straight; on Good ground at Galway's flat 7f, this shape rewards those who have saved ground and energy while still travelling close to the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Strong Finisher
scenarios.trigger: If Star Glory sets too strong a tempo early and ties up in the final furlong, allowing a hold-up runner to reel them in.
scenarios.body: A fast early fractions from Star Glory sap the leaders in the straight, opening the door for a horse held up off the pace to produce a sustained late run; this is the scenario most likely to produce a winner from further back, but it requires a genuinely honest gallop that the pace data here does not strongly suggest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow Burn, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively modest and the field compresses, turning the race into a sprint up the straight from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A modest early tempo means the whole field travels in a tight bunch and the race becomes a flat-out sprint home; unraced or lightly raced types like Gabby Hayes and Someday Somewhere who may possess raw speed could benefit from a pure dash, as experience and positional craft matter less.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds All
scenarios.trigger: If Star Glory's tempo is perfectly judged and it simply outstays everything from the front without being challenged or caught.
scenarios.body: Star Glory commands throughout, never asked a question until the straight and finding enough under pressure to hold the prominent horses who close late; this scenario is discounted because the STYLE_FIT tag signals Star Glory is racing somewhat out of role under this mapping and true hold-up types in the field could emerge more effectively than indicated.

watchPoints.text: Seaxburh holds the strongest profile for this race shape — O'Brien yard, McMonagle booked, two placed efforts over exactly 7f Good — watch whether she gets a smooth prominent position tracking Star Glory, as any traffic trouble early would significantly compromise her chance.

Star Glory sets the tempo for the entire field; if Chris Hayes elects to push on more aggressively than expected, the pace could become genuinely contested and undermine the prominent runners — watch the opening two furlongs to gauge whether this is a true solo lead or a forced one.

Hypiradon is a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield due to field congestion; watch whether Rory Cleary attempts to drop it out to find its natural position or is forced to race prominently, as either scenario represents a compromise and could lead to interference or a wide run in the straight.

Gabby Hayes is a Noel Meade debutante with no going data — watch the market and paddock closely, as unexposed two-year-olds from powerful yards on good ground can spring surprises when sent off at a price that reflects ignorance rather than ability.

The lightly raced trio of Miss Cornelia, Gabby Hayes, and Someday Somewhere all carry unknown or unpredictable tactical styles — watch how they jump and settle in the first furlong, as an unexpectedly keen or slowly away runner from this group could disrupt the anticipated shape behind Star Glory.

races.name: Village Salthill Handicap

runners_data.name: Iamimmaculate
runners_data.note: Sits just off the pace naturally and has two recent placings on Good or Soft ground over 8-10f; Dylan Browne McMonagle takes a useful booking and the step to 10f-plus suits this progressive 3yo who looks likely to secure a forward pitch here

runners_data.name: Mr Ballynonty
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner fitted with a hood who has run exclusively on Good going over 10-12f; W J Lee rides and the trainer is in decent recent form (2/31 in 14 days), but three Good-ground runs without a win and a fade record from the front raises questions at this trip

runners_data.name: Blue Blue Moon
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's 3yo is a hold-up type who has finished fifth on Good ground twice at 12f; Patrick McGettigan (5lb claimer) rides and the horse's recent form figures of 5-7-5 suggest it struggles to land a telling blow

runners_data.name: Felix Somary

runners_data.name: Snow Princess
runners_data.note: Co-front-runner who has been freshened up (8 days since last run) and has placed on Soft over 8f; James Ryan's mount has not won on Good ground across four recent tries and may find the sustained pace competition with Mr Ballynonty costly over this longer trip

runners_data.name: Good Man Jack
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by Patrick Magee who has finished eighth or worse in three of last four starts; the two-day turnaround is very quick, Good-ground form is weak (7/8 on similar) and the fade flag compounds the concern — hard to make a case

runners_data.name: Tharaka
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins' 3yo is a genuine hold-up type who placed on Good going over 7f and 8f; ran just two days ago which is a significant freshness query, but the trainer has a live 2/17 recent record and the horse has shown it can finish on Good ground when the pace suits

runners_data.name: Aquilla Star
runners_data.note: Has placed twice on Good-adjacent going and won on Heavy — a true hold-up horse whose natural rear position is compromised by the crowded back of the field; Siobhan Rutledge rides off a low mark of 64 and a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 tempers optimism unless it can find space

runners_data.name: Jp's Express
runners_data.note: Won last time out on Soft over 8f and placed on Good — Wesley Joyce (3lb claimer) keeps the ride for Michael Mulvany who is in excellent recent form (3/17 in 14 days); a natural hold-up type who has shown the ability to finish and carries only 131lbs despite the penalty

runners_data.name: Cisterna
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides this hold-up horse who has a win on Good ground (1/8f/GOO in recent hist) and strong overall Good-ground exposure (11/15 runs); displaced from its natural rear position by the congested field, its form credentials are real but the positional compromise is a genuine concern

runners_data.name: Unfamiliar
runners_data.note: Won on Good over 7f and has three soft-ground starts in recent form — a hold-up horse with a fade flag who is mapped out of its natural position; K Smith's yard is modest in the 14-day window (0/3) and the six-day turnaround following a zero finish last time asks questions

runners_data.name: Into Tomorrow
runners_data.note: Kieran Cotter's 3yo has only three runs and finished 4th on Heavy, 9th on Soft and 13th on Good — slim evidence, a fade flag, a 39-day break and a 7lb claimer aboard; true hold-up type displaced from its natural position, making a bold show hard to envisage on current data

runners_data.name: Nephin Mountain
runners_data.note: Won last time over 10f on Good and has placed on Good going previously; Michael Mulvany's yard is firing (3/17 in 14 days) and Terry Casey (7lb) takes off useful weight — a hold-up horse mapped away from its ideal position but the Good-ground win over a staying trip gives it residual claims if it can secure room

races.paceDynamic: Mr Ballynonty and Snow Princess are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this mile and a half on Good ground at Galway, creating a genuine, honest gallop rather than a false-run affair. With Iamimmaculate and Felix Somary also likely to press forward, the pace will be sustained and competitive through the early and middle stages, putting significant pressure on those making the running. The field contains more hold-up and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate cleanly — Aquilla Star, Cisterna, Unfamiliar, Into Tomorrow and Nephin Mountain are all natural hold-up horses redistributed into midfield positions because true rear-ground is unavailable; among those likely to secure a genuine prominent berth, Iamimmaculate and Felix Somary are best-placed. The tactical verdict is clear: a two-horse contested lead over a stamina-testing mile and a half on Good ground will burn through the front-runners and set this race up for a horse who can travel prominently just off the pace or launch a strong sustained run from midfield — a prominent-to-midfield profile that stays the trip well is favoured.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Ballynonty and Snow Princess fight each other for the lead and soften each other up, a prominent racer sitting just behind takes full advantage
scenarios.body: The two leaders expend energy in a duel through the first half-mile and are vulnerable from the home turn onward; a horse like Iamimmaculate, who sits just off the pace and has Good-ground form, is ideally positioned to pounce

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leaders Brave The Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Ballynonty or Snow Princess controls rather than contests the lead and the gallop settles into a true but manageable rhythm
scenarios.body: One of the two front-runners conserves enough energy through the middle stages to repel challenges in the straight; Mr Ballynonty's headgear (p) and recent Good-ground form over 10f gives him marginally the stronger platform to do so

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong end-to-end and the field strings out, allowing a well-handicapped midfield runner to pick up the pieces
scenarios.body: A truly run race over this trip can bring stamina-bred hold-up types into play in the closing stages; Tharaka has shown Good-ground form over sprint trips and could excel now stepping up, while Jp's Express won last time and carries a penalty

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Hold-Ups Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If several natural hold-up horses manage to secure wider positions and the pace collapses in the straight, enabling true closers to sweep through
scenarios.body: This scenario requires horses such as Cisterna, Aquilla Star or Nephin Mountain to overcome their mapped positions and race from where they are naturally comfortable, which the congested field makes unlikely; Cisterna does have winning Good-ground form and could surprise if she threads through

watchPoints.text: Mr Ballynonty and Snow Princess will clash for the lead from the jump — watch whether either horse breaks away cleanly to control the tempo or whether a sustained head-to-head duel develops, as this fundamentally determines how much the race burns through the whole field

Aquilla Star, Cisterna and Nephin Mountain are genuine hold-up horses mapped into midfield — watch whether they can filter to a comfortable position early or whether crowding forces them into a worse spot than their natural style demands

Jp's Express carries a penalty after winning last time and is trained by a yard with a 3/17 recent strike rate — watch whether Wesley Joyce can find cover quickly from a hold-up position and whether the horse's last-time-out win was a career peak or a progression marker

Tharaka and Good Man Jack both ran only two days ago — monitor market moves for either runner close to post time, as significant money on a very short turnaround would indicate stable confidence that the quick reappearance is deliberate

Iamimmaculate is the most prominent-style runner without a confirmed front-running tag — watch Dylan Browne McMonagle's positioning in the first furlong to see whether the horse secures the ideal sit just behind the two leaders or gets shuffled back into a less favourable spot

races.name: Fr. Breen Memorial (Pro/Am) Flat Race

runners_data.name: Farney Bridge
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer in excellent recent form (won 17 days ago at this 2m trip on Good), trained by John M Burke with a positive sim-going record of 2 from 2 on Good; amateur rider Ms Aine Connolly (7lb claim) keeps the weight manageable, and arriving late off a hot pace plays perfectly to this horse's strengths.

runners_data.name: Linford
runners_data.note: A prominent traveller trained by W P Mullins and ridden by Mr P W Mullins, this four-year-old has back-to-back wins including one on Good ground and arrives fresh after 55 days off; capable of sitting just behind the pace battle and picking off tiring leaders, making it one of the most naturally well-positioned profiles in the field.

runners_data.name: Mindyourheadmike
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner who will press for the early lead against Caislean Gear, with a Good-ground win on record; the 80-day absence is a query, and if forced to fight for every yard of the first mile there is a real stamina risk approaching the Galway finish under Mr D McGill (7lb claim).

runners_data.name: Caislean Gear
runners_data.note: The other designated pace-setter, freshly returned 17 days ago and in form (241 recent), with a Good-ground win over this exact trip; the horse has quality and recency on its side, and if it can assert early and avoid an exhausting duel, it becomes a more serious player in the finish than the pace-map might suggest.

runners_data.name: Reafadda
runners_data.note: A four-year-old lightly raced with no meaningful form data available and an unknown going profile — ridden by the experienced Mr H C Swan, which offers some compensation, but the complete absence of a last-run date and no style classification makes this a genuine unknown who must be treated with caution.

runners_data.name: Back In Favour
runners_data.note: Tagged as a hold-up performer but flagged for fading in the finish, with headgear (h) and a worrying recent form string including an eighth last time out on Good; the one piece of encouragement is a sim-going record that shows positional ability, but the finishing pattern is a significant concern against horses with more reliable late acceleration.

runners_data.name: The Two Mary's
runners_data.note: Another lightly raced unknown with an unclassified style, a poor recent form string (FP-) and 105 days off the track — the longest layoff in the field; trained by John Joseph Hanlon and ridden by a 7lb claimer, this runner carries the most uncertainty of any in the race and cannot be reliably placed within any scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Mindyourheadmike and Caislean Gear are both confirmed front-runners over this 2m trip on Good turf at Galway, meaning the early exchanges will be contested rather than processed at a steady clip — both handlers will want their horse to control matters, and neither is likely to yield without a fight. That duel will set an honest, pressured gallop from the outset, burning off excess early pace and compressing the race into a test of stamina and resolution in the final half-mile of Galway's stiff finish. The field also contains two genuine hold-up performers in Farney Bridge and Back In Favour, plus prominent-travelling Linford, so there will be horses arriving from off the pace into what should be a genuinely strung-out field by halfway. This race shape most clearly favours hold-up and late-finishing profiles — horses who can bypass the pace battle and deploy fresh energy into tired rivals on the run-in — with Farney Bridge and Linford best positioned to capitalise given their form profiles and fit for this going.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Mindyourheadmike and Caislean Gear burn each other up through a genuinely contested early pace, leaving them vulnerable inside the final 3f.
scenarios.body: The stamina-sapping Galway finish will expose any horse who has spent themselves in a speed argument, and hold-up horses arriving with a clean run will find the leaders legless. Farney Bridge and Linford, both travelling comfortably off the pace, are the profiles most likely to reel in a toasted front pair.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Shakes Free
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners (most likely Caislean Gear) immediately asserts and the other concedes, allowing a measured, controlled lead at a fair gallop.
scenarios.body: A single leader setting a confident but sustainable pace removes the attrition of a head-to-head duel and gives the horse-in-front every chance to control the tempo and conserve enough energy for the Galway climb. Caislean Gear's recent win at this trip on Good and fresh legs (17 days off) make this horse the most credible solo leader if the dynamic settles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Carnage Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is chaotic enough to cause positional scrambling among the hold-up horses, leaving the outcome dependent on which runner finds clearest passage.
scenarios.body: The small field of seven reduces traffic risks, but a strung-out race with tired leaders and multiple closers converging simultaneously can produce a messy final furlong where the winner is decided by a clear run rather than class. Reafadda and The Two Mary's, both unknown quantities whose lightly-raced profiles are hard to fully discount, could emerge from obscurity in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Pair Survive Duel
scenarios.trigger: If both Mindyourheadmike and Caislean Gear prove fit and tough enough to absorb the early pressure and still have reserves to hold on in the finish.
scenarios.body: This requires both front-runners to be significantly better than their ratings and recent form suggest, which is the least likely outcome given the stiff Galway finale. Mindyourheadmike, who does hold a Good-ground win over the course trip, is the marginally better candidate here if this materialises.

watchPoints.text: Watch Mindyourheadmike and Caislean Gear in the first half-mile — if both jockeys commit fully to the lead, the resulting pace duel could dramatically inflate fractions and compromise both horses' finishing prospects, reshaping the entire race for closers.

Farney Bridge's hold-up style suits this pace shape well, but Ms Aine Connolly (7lb claim) is an amateur rider in a contested tactical race — any positional error in traffic or a tardy switch wide could cost crucial lengths at a crucial moment.

Linford arrives after a 55-day break under W P Mullins; match fitness after nearly two months off is worth monitoring through the mid-race, as a horse who is not fully wound up may travel well but empty quickly on the Galway climb.

Reafadda is ridden by Mr H C Swan, an experienced amateur, which adds a degree of tactical intelligence to an otherwise data-empty profile — Swan may exploit a soft position mid-race, so do not completely ignore this runner despite the information vacuum.

Back In Favour's headgear (hood) and pronounced tendency to fade suggest this horse's chance is almost entirely dependent on the pace being truly scorching; if Mindyourheadmike and Caislean Gear do burn each other up, the early gallop could briefly flatter Back In Favour before the familiar fade reasserts.
